review_notes: 78 existing definitions: 40 exact local-token substitutions and 38 reviewed structured edits. Includes the private pay_spectacle definition outside the prior native-definition census. No new native-function coverage or gameplay-equivalence claim.

Preserve Agonizing Remorse hand/grave retries, empty-zone fizzle and life-loss timing; Kroxa discard queries; Theros god devotion thresholds, saved/current type IDs, clone/cast versus change-type routing and restoration reads; One with the Stars attachment and type-change order.

Death helpers keep attachment/control checks, detach byte positions, early returns, source/callback context, pending counts, Anax affected-controller refresh, Athreos owner/exile tags, bounded storage and differing return-list ranges, and legacy cleanup.

Erebos payment loops keep life rechecks, repeated Decline behavior and Done handling. Erebos Intervention keeps its existing own-grave shroud branch. Breach keeps escape options, temporary hand bookkeeping, cage filtering, graveyard source lookup, payment, fizzle cleanup and sorcery override restoration.

M20 keeps Field of the Dead repeated name queries, Mystic Forge distinct availability/activation tests and cached dialog values, Chandra player scans and loyalty payment, Cavalier callbacks and Veil context reads. Moldervine keeps its recovered zero-card draw behavior; no new native semantic audit is claimed.

Tymaret target initialization uses memset for the same 152-byte targets[19] storage. Field of the Dead replaces byte-wise initialization of its six trailing integer slots with memset. Existing card-specific quirks in alpha-only definitions are retained.
One combined build follows. No new gameplay tests, historical replay, inventory regeneration or reccmp refresh.
verification_policy: Affected-file hashes and exact token checks for alpha-only edits; focused review for structured edits. Build separately after the combined batch. Inventories and reccmp deferred to a larger checkpoint.
scope: Readability cleanup of existing recovered definitions; no new native coverage or gameplay-equivalence claim.
